title: Julian päiväkirja
summary: "Julian päiväkirja" by Peter Nansen is a diary-form novel written in the early 20th century. It follows Julia Matilda Magens, a young woman in Copenhagen, as she records her constrained family life, her hunger for freedom and warmth, and the tug-of-war between a safe future with her dependable suitor Erkki and a dangerous fascination with a charismatic actor, Alfred Mörch. Domestic unease, social observation, and romantic longing shape her inner conflict. The opening of the novel presents Julia starting her diary with a vow of honesty, sketching a bleak routine with a frail, loving mother, an ailing, self-absorbed artist father, and a wayward brother, then savoring tender nightly talks with her mother about love. New Year’s brings both yearning and a letter from Erkki that promises return and a respectable life, which she imagines with irony as comfort and slow suffocation. A visit to her kindly grandmother contrasts warmth and plenty with the chill at home. A trip to see Suleima ignites a dream of rescue by a “white sheikh,” soon fixed on the actor Alfred Mörch; gossip about his conquests both repels and magnetizes her. She watches a neighbor’s secret love affairs from her window, projecting fantasies of risk and escape. When Erkki returns, his gentleness and public possessiveness grate on her, and she postpones a proposal while their talk about Mörch sparks tension. Finally, in a reckless impulse, she sends Mörch an anonymous note to meet at the station, swears she won’t go, and then hints she has done something “terrible,” leaving the beginning on a poised edge of transgression.
